title: State Signal (MQA)
universe: Companies at MQA or Engaged stage (mqa_lifecycle_stage) · Source: HubSpot
actionability_rule: actionable = no logged call/email/meeting (notes_last_contacted) in the last 60 days, or never contacted.
cadence: Weekly · Mondays (HubSpot numbers via DASH_ROUTINE.md PHASE 1.5); policy research + Starbridge RFP refresh on request or ~monthly (state-signal-refresh skill)
data_flags: 266 of 1781 MQA/Engaged companies (15%) have no state_st value set — shown as 'Unassigned', excluded from ranking.

Product tag is a STATE POLICY / PROCUREMENT signal (which inquirED product that state's real legislation, adoption cycle, or open RFP relates to) — NOT yet which product a specific warm HubSpot account is interested in. Asked Tim (RevOps) for a company-level `primary_product_signal` rollup on 2026-09-16 — pending.

All 50 states + DC now have real, WebSearch-verified policy research (2 rounds: 10 top-actionable states + a full 40-state sweep of the rest). Every claim has a real, checkable source URL — none fabricated. A handful of states (e.g. WY, VT on some dimensions) came back with an honest 'no verifiable signal found' rather than a stretched claim.

Starbridge (inquirED's buyer-intelligence tool) is now wired in: `starbridge_open_rfps` per watch state, and `top` RFP detail, come from live Starbridge Bridges (ELA RFPs, GF8 RFPs, IJ RFPs — 622 total rows scanned, 51 currently open/New or Saved). This is a real, concrete procurement signal, distinct from and stronger than state legislative policy alone.

Draft outreach emails on the account drill-down are TEMPLATES generated from each account's real HubSpot signal + the state's real policy context — starting points for a rep to personalize, not finished copy.

Warm Signals (Starbridge board-meeting bridges, added 2026-09-22): live-pulled via listBridgeRows from the 3 [MASTER] Warm Signals bridges (GFE/IJ/Inkwell), scoped to rows Added to Bridge in the trailing 90 days (>= 2026-06-24) with Status New/Saved -- 3,104 rows in that window, of which only 11 clear the Meeting_Score >= 10 quality bar (score shown as-is, uncapped -- Starbridge's own scoring prompt is documented 1-10 but the raw AI output isn't bounded there in practice). Meeting Score (opportunity quality) is a different column from Match Score (bridge-scope confidence, 1-5ish) -- only Meeting Score is used for filtering/display here. Per-account matching used HubSpot COMPANY.starbridge_id = Starbridge buyerId (72 of the ~100 tracked MQA/Engaged accounts across the 10 top_states have a starbridge_id; only 1, Byram Hills High School/NY, currently clears the score>=10 bar) -- that lookup was NOT time-boxed, so it covers the full bridge history, not just 90 days. The remaining 10 qualifying rows are real board-meeting signal for districts outside the tracked MQA account list -- worth a look even though they haven't been cross-checked against full HubSpot company records. No personal contact data pulled into this dashboard from Warm Signals, per existing no-PII convention.

warm_signal.meeting: Byram Hills School District Board Goals 2026-2027
relevance: The Byram Hills Board of Education adopted 2026-27 goals that include preparing for a prekindergarten launch in 2028.
District planning for the launch includes studying research-informed prekindergarten curriculum and instruction.
The district plans to develop a prekindergarten curricular vision and create a scope-and-sequence.
The Board will determine the budgetary impact of the pre-K mandate while planning for providers, space, and future budgets.
warm_signal.talking_points:
**PreK Launch in 2028 – Early Curriculum Evaluation Phase**  
Byram Hills is actively planning its PreK program for a 2028 rollout. The board is currently studying research-informed curricula, developing a vision, and creating a scope-and-sequence. No curriculum has been selected yet, leaving the door open for early engagement.

**Emphasis on Integrated, Knowledge-Building Learning**  
The district’s goals stress content-rich, cross-disciplinary learning—integrating literacy, science, and social-emotional development. This aligns directly with Great First Eight’s approach of building vocabulary and background knowledge through cohesive, connected instruction.

**No Competing PreK Curriculum Adopted for 2026/27**  
As of now, there is no PreK curriculum adopted for the upcoming school year. The district is still in the research phase, so no competitor currently holds the PreK space. (K-5 literacy adoptions like Arts & Letters and UFLI exist, but not for PreK.)

HI.headline: Hawaii's Ready Keiki initiative (unveiled Jan 2023) grew public Pre-K from 37 classrooms (2022-23) to 92 classrooms across 74 DOE campuses (2024-25), en route to 50% of unserved 3-4 year-olds by 2027.
HI.detail: Advances Act 46 (2020) commitment to universal Pre-K by 2032. 1,637 children enrolled in state-funded preschool 2024-25, up 611 from prior year. Plan for 465 total new classrooms by 2032.
HI.outreach_angle: Hawaii DOE is standing up dozens of new public Pre-K classrooms every year; ask what curriculum is being selected for newly funded classrooms - a fresh Pre-K decision point for GF8.

sources.title: VNR - Ready Keiki Expands Public Pre-K Access

ME.headline: Maine's K-8 social studies standards revision stalled in 2024 (legislature declined to authorize the draft); 2025 lawmakers created a two-year Maine Learning Results Taskforce (LD 1701) to re-envision PK-12 standards, pausing the regular review cycle.
ME.detail: DOE Steering Committee had drafted revised Civics, Economics, Geography, History standards since 2023. Taskforce must report to the legislature's Education Committee by January 15, 2026, before any new standards finalized.
ME.outreach_angle: Maine's social studies standards are openly in flux; a good moment to introduce Inquiry Journeys as curriculum districts can pilot now, ahead of the Taskforce's recommendations.

sources.title: Maine DOE - Maine Learning Results Taskforce

DC.headline: The DC State Board of Education unanimously adopted revised K-12 social studies standards June 21, 2023, the District's first update in 17 years.
DC.detail: Review ran Feb 2021-Feb 2023. Separately, DC's Early Literacy Education Task Force Recommendations Amendment Act of 2024 requires LEAs adopt a science-based reading curriculum for SY2024-25 and kindergarten teachers complete literacy training by start of SY2026.
DC.outreach_angle: DC's social studies standards were untouched for 17 years before the 2023 rewrite; ask how the curriculum review against new standards is going and where Inquiry Journeys fits.

sources.title: OSSE Adopts New Social Studies Standards for District of Columbia Students

KS.headline: Kansas SB 438 (the Kansas Blueprint for Literacy), signed April 25, 2024, bans three-cueing and visual-memory-based reading materials in K-12 classrooms effective July 1, 2025.
KS.detail: SB 438 designates the science of reading as the state's official Tier 1 literacy methodology and, as of July 1, 2025, prohibits any textbook relying on three-cueing/visual memory for word recognition. Funds $10M for statewide teacher upskilling by 2030.
KS.outreach_angle: Kansas districts are now out of compliance with SB 438 if their K-2 ELA materials rely on three-cueing (banned since July 1, 2025) - Inkwell's structured-literacy design fills that compliance gap.

sources.title: Governor Kelly Signs Bipartisan Bill Establishing the Kansas Blueprint for Literacy
2024 Session Laws of Kansas, Chapter 82: Senate Bill 438

LA.headline: Louisiana's BESE approved revised K-12 English Language Arts standards on April 13, 2026, with stronger phonics/science-of-reading emphasis, effective the 2027-2028 school year.
LA.detail: Recommended by State Superintendent Cade Brumley from a standards review begun 2024 (ELA standards last updated 2015-16). LDOE will support districts with training and instructional material reviews ahead of the 2027-28 rollout.
LA.outreach_angle: Louisiana's April 2026 K-12 ELA standards take effect 2027-28 and sharply raise the bar on phonics - districts will review K-2 ELA curriculum well ahead of that date; Inkwell maps directly onto the new standards.

sources.title: Louisiana Strengthens Classroom Focus on the Science of Reading (LDOE)

MD.headline: Maryland's State Board voted January 23, 2024 to mandate Science of Reading-aligned instruction statewide, formalized October 2024, effective SY2024-25; revised MCCRS ELA standards + a new HQIM adoption framework followed in July 2025.
MD.detail: Requires phonics/fluency/vocabulary/comprehension-based instruction, K-3 universal screeners (new approved-screener list effective SY2025-26), science-of-reading proficiency for educator licensure from July 2025. Districts are actively re-evaluating K-5 ELA curriculum against the new HQIM framework.
MD.outreach_angle: Ask whether the district's current K-2 ELA materials have been benchmarked against Maryland's new HQIM rubric; Inkwell is purpose-built for science-of-reading compliance.

sources.title: State Board Calls for the Adoption of Science of Reading Statewide - MSDE
Maryland College and Career Ready Standards in ELA (revised, approved July 2025)

MO.headline: Missouri Gov. Kehoe signed omnibus bill SB 68 on July 9, 2025 (effective Aug 28, 2025), making phonics the mandatory primary word-reading strategy statewide and barring three-cueing.
MO.detail: Amends Section 170.014 RSMo; builds on 2022 'Read, Lead, Exceed' reforms (SB 681) and K-3 twice-yearly screening. DESE published Evidence-Based Reading Instructional Materials (EBRIP) guidance in 2025 identifying vetted K-5 reading curriculum.
MO.outreach_angle: Ask whether the district's current K-2 reading curriculum still relies on three-cueing methods now prohibited by SB 68; position Inkwell as evidence-based and phonics-forward.

sources.title: Governor Signs Wide-Ranging Education Legislation - Missouri DESE
Evidence-Based Reading Instructional Materials (EBRIP) Guidance 2025 - Missouri DESE

DE.headline: Gov. Meyer signed Delaware's FY2027 budget June 30, 2026, raising early-childhood (Purchase of Care) investment to $107.3M (from $76.3M FY26), plus $8M one-time for pre-K expansion, part of a stated 40%-by-2028 public pre-K enrollment goal.
DE.detail: Includes a 10% provider reimbursement increase and expanded income eligibility (200%->225% FPL). Follows an October 2025 declared 'literacy emergency' (2024 NAEP data) and a new Early Literacy Plan with $10M+ toward Science-of-Reading adoption and 'Bridge to Practice' grants.
DE.outreach_angle: Cite Delaware's FY27 early-childhood funding increase and 40%-by-2028 pre-K goal to open a conversation about curriculum for expanding/new PreK-TK classrooms - Great First Eight fits districts standing up new state-supported seats. Separately, ask whether the district has applied for Bridge to Practice literacy grant funding for Inkwell.

Delaware announces Early Literacy Plan - State of Delaware News

NM.headline: New Mexico has a standing universal K-3 dyslexia-screening/structured-literacy law (2019 SB398); a 2024 push (SB242) to embed structured literacy into teacher-prep stalled but is expected to return.
NM.detail: Districts already universally screen 1st graders for dyslexia and implement structured-literacy PD plans. SB242 (2024) would have required colleges of education to teach structured literacy; blocked in House Education Committee.
NM.outreach_angle: Position Inkwell's explicit, systematic K-2 ELA instruction as the curriculum districts will already be equipped to defend if a stronger structured-literacy mandate returns.

sources.title: New Mexico Statutes Chapter 22A - Literacy for Children at Risk

NC.headline: North Carolina's 2021 Excellent Public Schools Act mandated science-of-reading K-5 instruction and funded LETRS training for ~44,000 teachers; a new ELA Standard Course of Study is approved for SY2027-28.
NC.detail: $114M funded LETRS PD; declining below-benchmark reading rates 2022-2024. Current 2017 ELA standards remain through 2026-27; new 2026 standards take effect 2027-28.
NC.outreach_angle: Flag that the new ELA Standard Course of Study (effective 2027-28) is the cue to start evaluating core K-2 ELA materials now; Inkwell built for the structured-literacy instruction teachers are already trained in.

sources.title: North Carolina science of reading instruction bill, explained - EdNC

ND.headline: North Dakota is rewriting its K-12 Social Studies standards, Draft 1 published for public comment March 16-April 17, 2026; ELA standards were updated 2023 for science-of-reading alignment.
ND.detail: Full draft rewrite (standards last set August 2019) for public comment spring 2026. K-3 teachers/principals required (NDCC 15.1-21) to train in explicit, systematic science-based reading instruction.
ND.outreach_angle: Get in front of district curriculum committees now, before materials lock to the old 2019 standards; Inquiry Journeys ready to map to whatever's finalized.

sources.title: North Dakota Social Studies Content Standards - Draft 1

OH.headline: Ohio's 2023 House Bill 33 required every district adopt a state-approved, science-of-reading-aligned core ELA curriculum for PreK-5 by SY2024-25, backed by $168M, and banned three-cueing.
OH.detail: ODEW published an approved K-5 core list (Feb-Mar 2024) incl. CKLA, EL Education, Wit & Wisdom, Being a Reader. Most teachers/admins had to complete science-of-reading training by June 30, 2025.
OH.outreach_angle: Ask directly whether the district's current core curriculum is actually on Ohio's approved list - a district off that list is technically out of compliance.

sources.title: Updated list of approved core curriculum - Ohio Dept of Education and Workforce

OK.headline: Oklahoma Supreme Court struck down the state's 2025 social studies standards Dec 16, 2025 (Open Meetings Act violation); replacement 2026 standards approved March 26, 2026 still need legislative approval.
OK.detail: 5-4 ruling found the board voted on content not publicly posted beforehand. Reverts to 2019 standards meanwhile. Separately, Strong Readers Act (SB362, June 2024) mandates dyslexia screening, evidence-based K-3 reading, bans three-cueing from SY2025-26.
OK.outreach_angle: Districts are stuck buying curriculum against a moving standards target; position Inquiry Journeys as standards-agnostic, inquiry-based content built to adapt rather than be re-bought every time standards shift.

sources.title: Oklahoma Supreme Court strikes down controversial social studies standards - K-12 Dive

RI.headline: Rhode Island's Right to Read Act (2019) hit implementation deadlines 2023-2024 requiring educator-prep programs prove Science of Reading/Structured Literacy training; revised K-12 social studies standards endorsed Feb 2023.
RI.detail: RIDE-approved prep programs had to publicly post their SoR training approach by June 30, 2024. Also has real live RFPs: MPA 636 (K-12 social studies curriculum + PL, C3 Framework, LEAs align by SY26-27) and MPA 581 (PreK-12 curriculum-based PL) - both open per Starbridge.
RI.outreach_angle: Ask whether current core ELA curriculum reflects the Science of Reading/Structured Literacy training baked into every new RI teacher's prep program.

sources.title: The Rhode Island Right to Read Act - RIDE

SD.headline: South Dakota's State Board adopted new phonics-based ELA standards April 14, 2025, explicitly aligned to the science of reading, full implementation SY2025-26.
SD.detail: South Dakota has NO state-level instructional materials adoption process - all curriculum review is district-level, so with brand-new standards districts are actively re-evaluating core reading materials.
SD.outreach_angle: Since SD leaves curriculum vetting entirely to districts with no state adoption list, ask directly whether current core reading program has been checked against the new standards.

sources.title: South Dakota English Language Arts Standards Adopted April 14, 2025

past_campaigns.ctr: 8.08% on email 1, the best first-email number of the three campaigns

takeaways: Verify the sending inbox stays connected at enrollment and again partway through - this campaign lost most of its back half to a disconnect nobody caught for weeks.
Two lessons from Iowa (naming districts, an SDR handoff at email 4) weren't applied here in time - carry lessons forward campaign to campaign, not just into a document.
Filter the send list to public K-12 contacts only - the one reply this campaign got was an opt-out from a private-school teacher.

past_campaigns_note: Real figures from inquirED's Fall 2025-2026 Account-Driven Campaign brief and its Iowa/South Carolina post-mortems. Personal names excluded. Kentucky ran a full campaign (Sept 2025) but was never given a post-mortem; a 2024 SC outreach effort and an early Oregon sequence were never run as measured campaigns — none of the three shown here rather than displayed as empty rows.
outreach_playbook: Name specific in-state districts by the second or third email — the single strongest predictor of opens and clicks across every past account-driven state campaign run to date.
Write a multi-email sequence, not a single send.
Tag every send with UTMs and set an explicit SDR handoff trigger from the start.

A state with both real policy signal AND an open Starbridge RFP is the strongest kind of watch-state — the RFP names a live, dated buying process; treat it as a hard deadline, not just a talking point.

For a watch-state with an existing product relationship, frame the new product as an expansion tied to the existing renewal/adoption-cycle window — confirm that window with Sales/Customer Success before drafting.
For a cold-start watch-state with no existing footprint, plan for a longer ramp — there's no warm relationship to open the door.

top.meeting: Cupertino Union Elementary School District Local Control and Accountability Plan 2026-2027
relevance: Cupertino Union School District reports that Transitional Kindergarten expansion is affecting its budget alongside the expiration of one-time COVID funds and loss of its local parcel tax.
The district’s “Welcome to TK Events” sign-ups increased from 404 in 2024-2025 to 687 in 2025-2026.
CUSD plans to adopt new mathematics instructional materials through teacher evaluation, piloting, and recommendations.
The mathematics adoption process includes initial professional development in 2026-2027, completion by the end of 2027-2028, and a $29,000 budget allocation.
top.talking_points:
**TK Expansion and Financial Strain**: Cupertino Union School District is expanding Transitional Kindergarten, but this coincides with the loss of a local parcel tax, expiration of one-time COVID funds, and approved staff reductions for 2026-27. This financial pressure makes cost-effective, comprehensive curriculum solutions essential.

**Curriculum Adoption in Progress**: The district is currently undergoing a math curriculum adoption for 2026-27. However, no PreK/TK curriculum selection is referenced in the LCAP, leaving a gap for a knowledge-building, integrated curriculum like Great First Eight that addresses early learning holistically.

**Alignment with District Priorities**: The LCAP emphasizes future-ready learning, Portrait of a Learner competencies, and whole-child development. A curriculum that builds vocabulary, background knowledge, and foundational skills across subjects directly supports these goals, aligning well with the district's strategic focus.

top.meeting: Glendale Unified School District Local Control and Accountability Plan 2026-2027
relevance: Glendale Unified recently adopted K-8 social science instructional materials, with educators attending vendor presentations and participating in teacher-team selection.
Parent and guardian curriculum review committees continued meeting during 2025-2026 to provide input on elementary and secondary instructional-material adoptions.
The district identified culturally relevant curriculum emphasizing inclusion as a priority for its instructional program.
Glendale Unified also planned increased professional development to support implementation of academic standards.
The LCAP does not identify a timeline or commitment for the district’s next elementary social studies adoption.
top.talking_points:
**Curriculum Adoption Already In Place** – Glendale Unified has already adopted K-8 social science instructional materials for the 2026-2027 school year, indicating a competing curriculum has been selected.

**Equity and Academic Gaps** – The LCAP prioritizes closing achievement gaps for English learners, low-income, and foster youth. Social science curricula must be culturally responsive and support accelerated learning for these student groups.

**Complex Adoption & Review Process** – GUSD uses a rigorous vetting process with parent/guardian committees and library review to evaluate materials. Any new curriculum must align with strict local standards and community expectations, making entry challenging.

top.meeting: Azusa Unified School District Local Control and Accountability Plan 2026-2027
relevance: Early childhood education programs include Transitional Kindergarten alignment to grades K–3 with a planned $1,533,716 allocation.
TK enrollment growth required balancing space and staffing while integrating new preschool and TK teachers into professional development.
District local TK assessment targets show 2026 math performance increasing to 86% for all students.
top.talking_points:
**Significant Investment in TK Expansion and K-3 Alignment**  
Azusa USD allocates $1.53M in 2026-2027 for early childhood education, adding TK classrooms and aligning preschool/TK curriculum with grades K-3 to ensure smooth transitions. This creates a need for a comprehensive, knowledge-building curriculum that integrates literacy, math, science, and social studies.

**Focus on Early Literacy and Math with Data-Driven Outcomes**  
The district tracks TK math proficiency (rising from 80% to 86%), underscoring a strong emphasis on measurable foundational skills. They invest in professional learning (SEAL) and instructional aides to reduce student-to-adult ratios, highlighting a need for content-rich, integrated curricula that maximize instructional time.

**No Specific Competing Curriculum Identified**  
The LCAP does not name a commercial PreK/TK curriculum; instead, they rely on internal alignment and SEAL professional development. There is no evidence of an adopted competing product, leaving an open opportunity for Great First Eight to be presented as a cohesive, all-subject solution.

top.meeting: Carlsbad Unified School District Local Control and Accountability Plan 2026-2027
relevance: Instructional materials action includes “new instructional materials in Science and Social Studies” for 2026–2027.
“Instructional materials” are funded with $1,693,703 under Goal 2 Action 2.3.
Goal 2 emphasizes standards-aligned materials, instruction, and technology in a safe environment.
top.talking_points:
**$1.7M Investment in New Science & Social Studies Materials**  
Carlsbad Unified School District has allocated $1.7 million for new instructional materials in science and social studies for the 2026–2027 school year. This signals a competitive procurement process, and a competing curriculum may already be under consideration.

**Focus on Equity and Unduplicated Student Support**  
The LCAP prioritizes improving outcomes for Long-Term English Learners and socioeconomically disadvantaged students, who show low performance in ELA, Math, and Science. The district seeks culturally responsive materials and professional development to close gaps.

**Emphasis on Digital Resources and Teacher Training**  
Planned spending includes over $1.9M on digital hardware/software and $1.1M on instructional materials. With 96% of staff rating PD as relevant, the district values integrated digital solutions paired with robust teacher support.

top.meeting: Cypress School District Local Control and Accountability Plan 2026-2027
relevance: Full-day Transitional Kindergarten expansion planned for English learners, foster youth, and low-income students.
$1,117,167 budgeted for “Full Day Transitional Kindergarten and Kindergarten.”
TK program targets early literacy, numeracy, and integrated language development.
DRDP Benchmark Assessment data cited for TK/K program monitoring.
top.talking_points:
- **Full-Day TK Expansion with $1.1M Budget**: Cypress SD is investing heavily in full-day TK and Kindergarten (Action 1.8) to close early achievement gaps, particularly for English learners and low-income students. They seek a cohesive, content-rich curriculum that maximizes instructional time—an ideal entry point for Great First Eight.

- **Persistent Achievement Gaps Drive Curriculum Need**: Despite progress, gaps persist in ELA and math for unduplicated pupils. The district’s focus on early literacy, numeracy, and language development signals a need for integrated, knowledge-building PreK/TK materials.

- **No Single Competing Curriculum Identified for 2026/27**: The LCAP references multiple supplemental tools (Renaissance, Lexia, Heggerty) but no comprehensive, adopted PreK/TK core curriculum. This presents an opportunity for Great First Eight to fill the gap.

top.meeting: Byram Hills School District Board Goals 2026-2027
relevance: The Byram Hills Board of Education adopted 2026-27 goals that include preparing for a prekindergarten launch in 2028.
District planning for the launch includes studying research-informed prekindergarten curriculum and instruction.
The district plans to develop a prekindergarten curricular vision and create a scope-and-sequence.
The Board will determine the budgetary impact of the pre-K mandate while planning for providers, space, and future budgets.
top.talking_points:
**PreK Launch in 2028 – Early Curriculum Evaluation Phase**  
Byram Hills is actively planning its PreK program for a 2028 rollout. The board is currently studying research-informed curricula, developing a vision, and creating a scope-and-sequence. No curriculum has been selected yet, leaving the door open for early engagement.

**Emphasis on Integrated, Knowledge-Building Learning**  
The district’s goals stress content-rich, cross-disciplinary learning—integrating literacy, science, and social-emotional development. This aligns directly with Great First Eight’s approach of building vocabulary and background knowledge through cohesive, connected instruction.

**No Competing PreK Curriculum Adopted for 2026/27**  
As of now, there is no PreK curriculum adopted for the upcoming school year. The district is still in the research phase, so no competitor currently holds the PreK space. (K-5 literacy adoptions like Arts & Letters and UFLI exist, but not for PreK.)

top.meeting: Oak Park Board Of Education District 97 Regular Meeting
relevance: Early childhood curricular pilots include "Every Child Ready" and "Great First Eight" for evaluation and recommendation.
Professional learning and evaluation of early childhood pilots are planned to lead to a recommendation.
Core Instruction and Curriculum reports include Responsive Classroom (K–5) and Bridges Math (K–5) updates.
top.talking_points:
**Active PreK/TK Curriculum Pilots**  
Oak Park SD 97 is currently piloting both *Every Child Ready* and *Great First Eight* for early childhood programs. Professional learning and formal evaluation of these pilots will drive a recommendation, signaling an active decision window where inquirED can showcase Great First Eight's integrated, knowledge-building approach.

**Budget Pressures & Cost Sensitivity**  
The board reviewed an FY27 budget with intentional deficit spending, a 5% expense increase (health insurance, out-of-district tuition, capital improvements), and a focus on maintaining a balanced budget (138 reserve days). Cost-effectiveness and alignment with fiscal constraints will be key factors in curriculum adoption.

**No Competing Adoption Yet**  
No competing PreK/TK curriculum has been formally selected for 2026/27. While *Every Child Ready* is a direct competitor in the pilot, the final choice remains pending. This open evaluation period presents a clear opportunity to differentiate Great First Eight's coherent, content-rich model.

relevance: Ashland School Board initiated “core instructional materials” adoption for Social Science, targeting K-5 standards alignment.
Adoption initiation was justified for compliance with the Division 22 Corrective Action Plan.
Board materials cite improved equity, accessibility, and instructional consistency as adoption drivers.
top.talking_points:
**Curriculum Adoption Initiated**: Ashland SD 5 is initiating a core instructional materials adoption for Social Science at this meeting, driven by a Division 22 Corrective Action Plan and new Oregon standards. This opens a formal review process for new curriculum.

**Structured Evaluation Process**: The district will form a curriculum committee to review data, develop criteria, and present materials for board and public feedback, with adoption expected by May 2027. This indicates a defined timeline for vendor engagement.

**No Existing Competitor Selected**: No competing curriculum has been chosen for 2026/27. The district is starting fresh, providing an opportunity for new vendors. They emphasize equity, accessibility (UDL), and alignment with standards, and have funding available.

top.meeting: Tanque Verde Unified School District Governing Board Governing Board Meeting Minutes
relevance: Tanque Verde Unified School District is planning a K-6 ELA curriculum adoption, with the formal process opening in January and final selections anticipated in spring.
The adoption timeline was reviewed during the district’s September 16, 2026 governing board meeting.
The State Board is expected to select an assessment provider for 2027-2028 and has issued a new RFP covering ELA, Math, and Science assessments.
top.talking_points:
**K-6 ELA Curriculum Adoption in Progress**  
TVUSD is actively evaluating a new K-6 ELA curriculum; the formal adoption window opens in January with selections expected in spring. This is a current, time-sensitive procurement cycle.

**State Accountability Shifts Impact Curriculum Choices**  
Starting Fall 2027, bonus points will no longer factor into letter grades, and the state is launching a new RFP for ELA, Math, and Science assessments for 2027–28. These changes will likely drive curriculum alignment priorities, creating a need for standards-based, integrated solutions like Inkwell.

**No Competing Curriculum Selected for 2026/27**  
The minutes contain no reference to any ELA curriculum already adopted or selected for the upcoming school year. The district is in the early evaluation stage, indicating an open opportunity for a K-2 core ELA program.
